items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Duet, a proactive agent app that works in the background
items.summary: On 21 October Anthropic opened a research preview of Claude Duet, a standalone app for iOS, Android and claude.ai in which Claude acts as a proactive agent. Every morning it sends a brief of the most important items across the user's connected apps. It checks those accounts every few hours and messages the user only when something needs attention. It runs on its own virtual machine with its own browser, so the user's laptop or phone does not need to be on. It asks for approval before it sends messages, makes payments, signs documents or deletes anything. It will not trade securities or move money between accounts, even with approval. Duet can use more than 6,000 connectors and plugins in the Claude Marketplace, including Gmail, Slack, QuickBooks, Stripe, HubSpot, Docusign and LinkedIn. It can make purchases through Stripe's Link with a virtual card. Access is by waitlist, starting with US Pro and Max subscribers, and Duet shares those plans' usage limits. Android Authority reports that it runs on Claude Opus 5.5. Anthropic says it is aimed at professionals and small-business owners.
items.why_it_matters: The AI assistant is moving from answering questions to monitoring email, finance and sales tools on its own, and only asking for approval before it acts. This puts Anthropic in direct competition with Meta Muse and the always-on agents from OpenAI and Google, and it raises new questions about trust and access control in working life.

items.title: Notion rebuilds its AI agents: 24-hour tasks, their own browser and a new credit system
items.summary: On 19 October Notion announced rebuilt agents. They get their own computer and browser and can work on a single task for more than 24 hours, up from five minutes. A new Auto model router picks a model per task. Notion says it gives results similar to Opus 5.5 and Astra at about 90 percent lower average cost across 20+ use cases. Agents run up to 50 percent faster, and Custom Agent runs cost about 30 percent less in testing. Users can connect a ChatGPT Plus, Pro or Go subscription to a personal Notion agent, and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) is in private alpha for Enterprise. Business and Enterprise seats get 1,500 Standard credits and 500 Select credits per month. Existing customers move to the new credit system on 2 November.

sources.name: Notion blog – Agents, rebuilt to do more for less

items.why_it_matters: Notion is widely used by students and in startups and consulting. Long-running agents and a model router that cuts costs show how productivity tools are becoming agent platforms, and the new credit model changes what teams pay for AI use.

items.title: Uber gives all 30,000 employees OpenAI's ChatGPT Work agent
items.summary: On 22 October Uber and OpenAI announced that all of Uber's roughly 30,000 employees worldwide get access to ChatGPT Work, the enterprise agent OpenAI launched in July. It follows a pilot with about 1,000 employees in finance, operations and product. Uber's VP of engineering, Sumanth Sukumar, says about 80 percent of early adopters were not engineers. In the pilot they analysed operational data, localised training materials and built dashboards. Developers keep using Codex. Uber has not disclosed the cost and says it will measure usage and outcomes before deploying AI more widely.
items.why_it_matters: This is one of the largest company-wide rollouts of an AI agent to date, and most users were outside engineering. It is a concrete example of how large companies are bringing agents into ordinary knowledge work, and of OpenAI's enterprise race with Anthropic.

items.title: Volkswagen has given Microsoft Copilot to more than 330,000 employees
items.summary: On 21 October Microsoft announced that Volkswagen Group has equipped more than 330,000 employees with Microsoft Copilot. The earlier Copilot Chat phase reached over 300,000 monthly active users. More than 26,000 agents were active across the group in the past month. Employees now use Copilot with Work IQ in engineering, production, procurement and sales. The two companies will also expand Volkswagen's data platform on Microsoft Fabric. The collaboration was presented at the Microsoft Frontier Tour in Cologne on 22 October.
items.why_it_matters: This is one of Europe's largest Copilot deployments, with concrete usage figures (300,000 monthly users, 26,000 agents). It is a useful reference point for anyone assessing the effect of AI in large industrial companies.

items.title: Perplexity Computer can now run entirely locally on a Mac
items.summary: On 20 October Perplexity made it possible to run the Computer agent entirely on a Mac, including the harness and orchestrator. It requires a recent Apple Silicon Mac with at least 36 GB of RAM. Users choose between Qwen 3.6 and PPLX Pro, a version of Qwen 3.6 that Perplexity has post-trained for Computer use. If the user authorises it, the agent can call one of more than 15 frontier models in the cloud. Code and tools run in an isolated sandbox. The feature is available to Pro, Max and Enterprise subscribers through the Perplexity Mac app.
items.why_it_matters: Local agents keep sensitive data such as email and client documents on the user's own machine and reduce credit spend. That is relevant for consulting and finance, where privacy and compliance often block cloud tools.

items.title: Google this week: Docs Live by voice, Meet translation in 63 languages and Gemini Notebook in the Gemini app
items.summary: Google Workspace rolled out a series of Gemini features from 19 to 23 October. Docs Live (21 October) lets mobile users dictate structured documents using context from Gmail, Drive and Chat. Real-time speech translation in Google Meet expanded to 63 languages with automatic language detection (22 October). Gemini Notebook became a Connected App in the Gemini app, so users can create notebooks and add sources from a chat (23 October). Gemini in Sheets can analyse BigQuery data in natural language and arrived on iOS. Google Chat now gets meeting recap cards with decisions and action items. For education, Gemini Notebook in Google Classroom gives teachers insight summaries of how students used assigned notebooks (19 October).
items.why_it_matters: These are the tools many students and businesses use every day. Voice-driven writing, multilingual meetings and AI insight for teachers in Classroom show that AI is being built directly into everyday office and teaching work.

items.title: ChatGPT gets locked chats with a PIN or Face ID
items.summary: On 20 October OpenAI began rolling out locked chats in ChatGPT for Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu. A locked chat is protected by a four-digit PIN or Face ID/Touch ID. It moves to a separate Locked Chats section and is hidden from history, pinned chats and search. With Memory on, locked chats have their own memory. Locking does not add end-to-end encryption or change data retention, and resetting the PIN permanently deletes all locked chats.
items.why_it_matters: Many people use ChatGPT for sensitive matters on shared or work devices. The feature gives practical protection, but users should know that it is not encryption and does not change how OpenAI stores data.

items.title: ChatGPT ads expand to 89 countries and over 100,000 advertisers
items.summary: On 21 October OpenAI announced that ads in ChatGPT are expanding to 26 more countries, for a total of 89. The new markets include 14 in Latin America, plus Nigeria, South Africa, Serbia, Ukraine, Bangladesh and Pakistan. More than 100,000 advertisers have used the platform, through partners or OpenAI's self-service Ads Manager. Ads appear only on the Free and Go plans. Personalised ads are initially unavailable in the EEA and Switzerland. Reporting says the ads business passed an annualised run rate of 1 billion dollars in August.
items.why_it_matters: Ads are becoming a real revenue stream for OpenAI and a new marketing channel. For Norwegian users the EEA restriction on personalised ads matters, as does the fact that only the free plans show ads.

items.title: Gemini's Personal Intelligence uses Maps history and reaches Android Auto, and Argon will replace Deep Think
items.summary: On 22 October Google expanded Personal Intelligence in the Gemini app so that it can use the user's Google Maps searches and saved places. It is opt-in and can be combined with Calendar, for example to suggest saved restaurants near the next meeting. The same week Personal Intelligence began rolling out to Android Auto, and it will reach cars with Google built-in over the coming months. AI Ultra subscribers were told that Gemini 4 Argon will "soon" replace Deep Think.
items.why_it_matters: Google is using its biggest advantage, personal data across Maps, Calendar and Gmail, to make Gemini more useful. That also makes privacy settings more important for users.

items.title: Microsoft removes eight Copilot actions from File Explorer in Windows 11
items.summary: Windows Latest reported on 21 October that Microsoft is retiring eight Copilot actions from the right-click menu in File Explorer: Summarize, Create FAQ, Compare Files, Ask a question, Explain image, Explain images, Compare images and Extract text. Microsoft calls it "simplifying usage". The removal starts in mid-November 2026 and should be complete by December. Copilot remains available through "Ask Copilot" and the OneDrive activity center. The change follows earlier rollbacks in Notepad, Snipping Tool, Photos and the taskbar amid the "Microslop" backlash.
items.why_it_matters: It shows that putting AI everywhere has met user resistance, and that even Microsoft is now cutting back where AI features do not add value.

items.title: Claude for Enterprise gets chat and Cowork in one experience, with an Efficient mode to control costs
items.summary: Anthropic has made the unified Chat and Cowork experience generally available for Claude Enterprise; the release log dates it 23 October. Admins get role-based access, connector policies, approval modes and usage controls. A new Efficient mode limits users to Sonnet and Haiku models, and new sessions start on Claude Sonnet 5.5 at low effort. The experience turns on by default on 16 November 2026 for organisations that have not changed the setting. It is not available to organisations with zero data retention, the HIPAA-ready configuration or customer-managed encryption keys.
items.why_it_matters: Large companies get tools to roll out agent-style AI widely while controlling costs, a topical issue after the reports of companies capping their AI spending per employee.
